offence_severity: Death (Section 302 IPC) with minimum 10 years and maximum life imprisonment or death
physical_harm: Victim was assaulted with an axe and later declared dead
number_of_offences: Four accused charged with Section 302 IPC read with Section 34 IPC; two convicted, two acquitted
premeditation_planning: Court found premeditated intention as the accused were armed and present at the scene with a clear plan
motive: Evil eye kept on the wife of one of the accused by the deceased
key_evidence_accepted: The presence of all the accused at 3.30 in the morning at the site with two of them holding an axe clearly shows a common intention in furtherance of what they were proposing to do.
witness_credibility: The witnesses were reliable, more so the wife of the deceased who was an eye witness and also related what the deceased stated to her.
trial_duration: Offence: 2nd and 3rd November, 2015; Trial judgment: 14.09.2017; High Court decision: 05.02.2019; Supreme Court decision: 28.07.2022
legal_representation: Akash Kakade, Somanatha Padhan, Swetab Kumar, Ashok Anand, Rakesh Kr. Singh, Bipin Bihari Singh, Advs. for the Appellants; Rahul Chitnis, Sachin Patil, Aaditya A. Pande, Geo Joseph, Ms. Shwetal Shepal, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered (No.79/2015 dated 03.11.2015), charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Acquittal of appellants; High Court: Reversed acquittal of appellants; Supreme Court: Appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that there was a common intention among all the accused to cause the death of the victim, supported by the presence of all four accused at the scene with weapons and the testimony of the wife of the deceased.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the appellants only held the deceased without participating in the actual assault or using a weapon, and thus should not be held liable for the murder.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle of constructive liability under Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, emphasizing the need for a common intention and participation in the criminal act.
precedent_relied_upon: Jasdeep Singh Alias Jassu v. State of Punjab (2022) 2 SCC 545 : 2022 (1) JT 96; Virendra Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2010) 8 SCC 407 : [2010] 9 SCR 772
